newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firmer on new economic pact.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firmer on new economic pact.

text.p: The Mexican peso relinquished some of its early strength, but still closed firmer on Monday.

Traders said initial strength was due to speculation abating after the ACE economic pact had been signed, and that the peso later pared its gains due to dealers buying dollars to close month-end positions.

"The market opened liquid as banks sold long (dollar) positions they had bought last week to hedge against the ACE," said a trader, referring to the Alliance for Economic Growth (ACE), a three-way pact on economic measures signed by government, business and labor leaders.

The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.1 and two centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8950/7.9040 and 7.8900/7.9000 per dollar. The 48-hour peso opened four centavos firmer at 7.8750/7.8850 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 4.5 centavos firmer at 7.8750/7.8850 per dollar.

The ACE agreed to minimum wage increases of 17 percent in December, along with hikes of up to 22 percent for electricity and fuel costs. The ACE also envisages growth and inflation of four and fifteen percent, respectively, for 1997.
Traders said that another reason for the peso ceding some ground in late trade was that stocks began to slide after midsession.
The blue chip IPC index was down 17.83 points, or 0.55 percent, at 3,215.45 when the foreign exchange market closed.
Traders said that Tuesday's trade in the foreign exchange market would be very much determined by the outlook for the primary Cetes auction to be held in the evening.
